P1.evidence: Read back the setter properly — 'I spoke to Kim. You had a conversation with him a few days ago, so he just gave me some brief information about you' — and then delivered a genuine four-part frame: 'I'm kind of an old-school guy, and I would like to hear it from you and get into more depth on where you're at right now, what have you tried, where are trying to get to, and if we can help you, actually, to get there.' He never asked for frame agreement, no 'does that work?', and the open question was implicit in the frame rather than asked; the prospect simply started talking.

P2.evidence: The second half of the baseline ran cleanly and the first half was not run at all. Injuries were asked directly — 'in terms of injuries, do you have any injuries right now or any limitations that are appearing in your body?' — as were diet ('second part, nutrition. And be honest, please. How does it look like for you right now?') and sleep, recovery and energy in one clean sweep. But age, height and weight were never asked: 52, 211 lb and the 230 lb peak all arrived because the prospect volunteered them, and height never surfaced at all. Occupation was never asked despite being unusually relevant here — the Army is the source of both a hard deadline and a fitness standard. Health conditions were never asked, so the cholesterol medication, the low testosterone, the prior antidepressants and the sleep study all arrived unprompted. Training frequency and current results were never asked.

P3.evidence: The bridge to why was the strongest moment of the call. 'What's your biggest why on this? Why do you want to actually do this? Because it's not something that you realized one week ago' followed by 'So why now?' produced the son — 18, Type 1 diabetic, already at his father's weight — and the line 'if I don't show him that I can change my body that looks like his into something that I'm proud of, he won't believe he can do it either.' The rep then drove it exactly as the script asks: 'you're not doing this only for yourself. But as an example, to your son. And that will get you through the hardship,' and reflected it back at the close of the pillar walkthrough — 'most importantly, showing up for your son. Yeah?' Surface goals were thinner: he asked the main-goal question well but never asked mobility-versus-strength-versus-energy, never asked what he wants to do physically but can't, and never asked who else this impacts — the son came out of 'why now', not out of that question.

P4.evidence: The best-run Phase 4 in this batch. 'What have you tried' was built into the opening frame and produced a detailed vShred post-mortem including three injuries and three rounds of physical therapy. The rep then probed the language rather than moving on — 'what do you mean the cycle of self-doubt? That's a strong way to put it' — which is what pulled the real gap out of the prospect in his own words: 'I always feel like I don't really have a focus, so because of the lack of focus, I don't see the results I'm hoping for, and then I get discouraged and stopped', and later 'you're telling me stuff I know, I just don't know how to implement them, per se.' The rep landed the scripted root-cause line almost verbatim off that: 'Look, if you would know how to implement them, you wouldn't be on a call with me today.' Only P4d is short — he never asked the direct 'what's the one thing actually getting in the way' question; the prospect assembled it himself.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was run, but the prospect supplied one unprompted in answer to 'why now?': 'I worry if I'm 52 and feeling like my health isn't where it should be... where am I going to be at 60, where am I going to be at 75. I think I'm just going to be worse off if I don't do something about it now.' The rep acknowledged it and moved on. He never asked whether that is something the prospect is willing to settle for, never asked why not, and never asked for a line in the sand. The nearest he came was 'we need to start now, not yesterday'. With a prospect who volunteers a negative trajectory, a medicated cholesterol result, an 18-year-old on the same path and an Army separating people for body fat, this was the cheapest urgency available on any call in the batch and none of it was converted into a commitment.

P6.evidence: The all-in question was asked properly and before anything was presented: 'I just wanted to ask you one last thing. If we can figure out all the details. Are you going to be fully committed to actually showing up and doing this freaking work?' It was then re-confirmed after the pillars and before the price — 'I already asked you, if we can figure out all the details, are you going to show up and be committed?' / '100%. 100%.' — so the rep had a clean verbal yes in hand at the moment of presenting. He never asked the belief question, whether the prospect thinks he can get there with the right structure and the right person in his corner; the prospect had effectively self-answered it earlier ('that's what I think I need at this point'), but the rep did not ask it.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and every step of Phase 11 was skipped. Payment was not collected and — the decisive failure — no link was sent even though the prospect asked for one: 'So, are you going to send me a link for payment and stuff?' answered with 'I need to get you onboarded and so on. So, do you have that right now with you?' The Trevor onboarding call was actively deferred rather than scheduled: 'this week it's going to be impossible because it's already Friday and tomorrow is holidays.' No agreement was sent or signed on the call — it was never mentioned. Nothing at all about the welcome email, the Skool community link or the onboarding questionnaire. What the rep did instead was book a second closing call for Monday at 10:00 Central and confirm the invite landed, which is real but is not any of the four steps.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered by the three-week Estonia deployment — 'I don't know if it makes more sense to start in August.' The rep did the single most useful thing available, which was to ask why rather than rebut: 'Why would you say it would make more sense to start in August?' That surfaced the real assumption, which was that the programme runs on live Zoom calls with Trevor, and correcting it dissolved the objection. None of the scripted moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now' — but the outcome was better than the script would have produced.

The money trigger was live and explicit — 'I don't think any of mine have 6,000 available on it. I'll have to look' and 'I'm going to have to move some funds around to get $6,000 on there' — and no part of the open wallet ran. No isolation question, no SHOULD I / HOW reframe, no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no number of cards, no available credit per card, no used-versus-available, no investments. The rep's entire response was to name an alternative payment instrument ('you can use the debit card, too... If you have it in your savings or checking account, that's totally fine') and then book a call three days out. Because no financial picture exists, nobody knows whether Monday's $6,000 is real.

ICP / age-fit objection, which has no scripted play. The prospect opened by disqualifying himself against Trevor's own advertising — 'one of his videos said he was looking for men between the ages of like 30 and 45... I don't want to waste your time if I'm not in your target audience' — and returned to it twice more, including 'I think I need to do a little bit on my own to prove I'm worthy of Trevor.' The rep handled it with a precedent anecdote about a 69-year-old and 'everybody that's coming in, they lack something', which worked, but the script offers nothing here and the underlying marketing contradiction is a company problem rather than a rep problem.

Clinical-fit gap, the same hole the playbook already records. The prospect is on prescribed statin therapy, has been offered hormone therapy, is mid-course in physical therapy for Achilles tendinitis, reports knee tenderness on volume squats and injured himself three times on his last programme. There is no scripted move for establishing medical clearance, so the rep instead treated the medications as targets to eliminate. A clinical screen belongs in the script at Phase 2 and does not exist.

notes: Phases 4 and 6 were run properly and the call earned a full-price verbal yes — then Phase 11 was not run at all and the prospect who asked for a payment link did not receive one. Coach exactly one thing: when a prospect says 'let's get that covered' and asks for a link, send the link on the call. Second priority, stop treating prescribed medication as something the programme removes; that is a clinical claim the rep is not in a position to make.
